sections.h2: Where is Hoover, Alabama, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Hoover is a city in north central Alabama that sits in two counties, Jefferson and Shelby, and belongs to the Birmingham metro area. It lies along the foothills of the Appalachian Mountains. If you are selling a house here, the first thing to confirm is which county holds your parcel, because that decides which probate office records the deed.

The city covers 50.326 square miles, and 0.972 of those are water. Downtown Birmingham is about 11 miles north by I-65 or US-31, and Montgomery is about 82 miles south. Hoover uses ten different ZIP codes, so the mailing city on a tax bill or listing does not always tell you the county.

  • County: Jefferson and Shelby
  • Metro: Birmingham
  • Land area: 49.354 square miles
  • Elevation: 495 feet
  • Government: mayor and a seven member city council

The Wikipedia profile of the city lists dozens of named communities inside the limits, among them Bluff Park, Riverchase, Ross Bridge, Greystone, Inverness, Trace Crossings, Shoal Creek, Lake Cyrus and Shades Mountain. Each has its own age of housing and its own buyer pool, which is why a flat answer about "a Hoover house" rarely holds.

sections.h2: How did Hoover grow into Alabama's sixth largest city?
sections.html:
Hoover was incorporated in 1967 and has grown by annexation and new subdivisions into the sixth largest city in Alabama. In 1970 the census counted 688 people. By 2020 it counted 92,606.

A big step came on September 8, 1980, when the city annexed the Riverchase business and residential community, which brought large office buildings and workers into the tax base. Later, the interchange where I-459 meets I-65 inside the city gave the area easier highway access.

The pace has slowed. The Census Bureau estimate for 2025 sits only about one percent above the 2020 count, so the explosive growth of the 1980s and 1990s is behind the city. A house in an older neighborhood now competes with newer ones built during that boom.

sections.h2: What are the largest employers in Hoover?
sections.html:
Regions Bank is the largest employer in Hoover, followed by Hoover City Schools and Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Alabama. These figures come from the city's 2022 financial report as summarized on Wikipedia.

The Riverchase Galleria complex, the Riverchase Office Park and retail centers such as Patton Creek and the Village at Lee Branch anchor the commercial side. For a seller, this mix of office, school and retail jobs means many households have steady local work, but a job change or relocation can still force a quick sale.

sections.h2: What do Hoover housing numbers show for sellers?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 39,008 housing units in Hoover and 36,799 households, with 5.7 percent of units vacant. That is a fairly full housing stock.

The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.3 percent, while the rental vacancy rate was 9.6 percent. About 54.7 percent of households were married couple households and 26.8 percent were one person households, so buyers range from families to people living alone.

The median age was 39.2, and 17.2 percent of residents were 65 or older. Owners who age in place, heirs who inherit a family house and people relocating for work are all common seller types in a city with this age profile. Houses in those situations often carry deferred repairs, which is where a buyer who purchases as-is can fit.

Hoover City Schools serves the city, with ten elementary schools, three middle schools and two high schools, Hoover High School and Spain Park High School. In the 2022 to 2023 year the system enrolled 13,557 students.

Spain Park received the National Blue Ribbon award in 2008. Rezoning in 2018 changed which grades attend Brock's Gap Intermediate and Bumpus Middle, so a family looking at an older listing may ask which zone it falls into.

For college, the Shelby-Hoover campus of Jefferson State Community College is in the city near Spain Park High School, and Faulkner University has a campus on Valleydale Road. The University of Alabama at Birmingham is roughly 8 to 10 miles away.

sections.h2: What roads and transit connect Hoover?
sections.html:
Two interstates, I-65 and I-459, cross Hoover, with a major interchange near the center of the city. U.S. 31 runs north and south through the middle, U.S. 280 serves the east, and State Route 150 runs east and west.

Valleydale Road links U.S. 31 and U.S. 280. The Birmingham-Jefferson County Transit Authority also serves the city.

sections.h2: How do property tax and deed recording work for a Hoover sale?
sections.html:
Alabama property taxes are due October 1 and are delinquent after December 31, according to the state Department of Revenue. If you sell in the fall, the buyer and seller usually settle that year's bill at closing, so ask the closing office how it will be split.

Alabama also charges a deed recording tax. Under Alabama Code 40-22-1, the tax is 50 cents for each $500 of value conveyed, and the deed must be accompanied by proof of the actual purchase price. The tax is paid before the instrument is received for record.

Hoover sits in Jefferson and Shelby Counties. The Jefferson County probate court has a Birmingham division at 716 North Richard Arrington Jr. Blvd. and a Bessemer division at 1801 3rd Avenue North, open 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays. Its staff say they cannot run a title search or prepare a deed, so that work goes to a title company or an attorney.

  • Taxes due October 1, delinquent after December 31
  • Deed tax: 50 cents per $500 of value
  • Recording office cannot search liens or draft deeds
  • Copies of recorded deeds are $1.00 per page at the record room

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Hoover house usually go?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Hoover follows the same legal steps as any other sale, minus the loan underwriting. A title company searches the title, the deed is prepared, the transfer tax is paid and the deed is recorded in the right county.

Sellers in a city this size often hold homes from different decades, and a buyer paying cash can purchase without a lender appraisal. That removes one common cause of delay. It does not remove liens, open tax bills or an unclear title, which should be sorted out before closing.

  • Confirm which county, Jefferson or Shelby, holds the parcel
  • Ask a title company to search for liens
  • Check that the current year's property tax is paid or prorated
  • Decide if you want repairs done first or want to sell as-is

faqs.q: Is Hoover in Jefferson County or Shelby County?
faqs.a: Both. Hoover spans Jefferson and Shelby Counties in north central Alabama, so a parcel can be in either. Check your tax bill or the county records to see which probate office will record your deed.

faqs.q: What is the population of Hoover, Alabama?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 92,606 people, and the 2025 Census Bureau estimate is 93,550. Hoover is the sixth largest city in Alabama.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Hoover?
faqs.a: October 1, and they become delinquent after December 31. These dates come from the Alabama Department of Revenue.

faqs.q: How much is the Alabama deed tax on a sale?
faqs.a: The state charges 50 cents for each $500 of value conveyed, or part of $500, under Alabama Code 40-22-1. Proof of the actual purchase price must accompany the deed.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Hoover house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Homes with deferred repairs sell to buyers who purchase as-is, and no repairs are required by law before listing. A title search and an up to date tax payment are still needed to close.

faqs.q: Who handles recording for Hoover deeds?
faqs.a: The probate court of the county where the parcel sits. For Jefferson County the recording office has Birmingham and Bessemer divisions and is open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
